gates.name: Workspace structure
gates.description: Workspace layout sanity: one instruction source per level, no unexpected nesting, no conflicting agent environments.
gates.pass_when: no drifted AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pairs, no nested repositories, project directories match the harnesses in use
gates.fail_when: an AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pair at one level is neither identical nor a pointer
gates.warn_when: a repository is nested inside another repository; project directories exist for several harnesses while at most one is active
evidence: harness dirs present: 1, active among them: 1
gates.recommendation: Fix the layout: one instruction source per level, no nested repositories, project dirs only for harnesses in use.

gates.name: Configuration integrity
gates.description: Configuration files parse and have no duplicate keys.
gates.pass_when: every configuration file parses and each key occurs once
gates.fail_when: a configuration file has a syntax error or duplicate keys
gates.warn_when: no configuration files were found at all
gates.recommendation: Fix or remove broken config files; keep one key per setting.

gates.name: Rules consistency
gates.description: Instruction files resolve, agree and stay within budgets.
gates.pass_when: no dead references, no drifted pairs, no boilerplate, files within the 16 KB benchmark and the 32768-byte chain budget
gates.fail_when: dead links, paths or commands; a drifted AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pair
gates.warn_when: generic boilerplate in auto-loaded context; an instruction file over 16 KB; the AGENTS.md chain over 32768 bytes
gates.recommendation: Repair dead references, merge drifted pairs, replace boilerplate with project-specific rules.

gates.name: Directory ownership and discoverability
gates.description: Every directory has a decided fate; valuable data sits under version control.
gates.pass_when: no heavy data directories outside git, no loose top-level folders
gates.fail_when: a heavy non-build directory sits outside every git repository
gates.warn_when: other top-level folders outside version control
gates.recommendation: Give every folder a fate: version control, archive or deletion.

gates.name: Skills and agent capabilities
gates.description: Skills have valid frontmatter, usable descriptions and synced copies.
gates.pass_when: frontmatter parses with the required fields, descriptions are under 1024 chars with triggers, copies are identical, references resolve
gates.fail_when: missing name or description, unparseable frontmatter, a description over 1024 chars, diverged copies of one skill
gates.warn_when: no trigger phrase in a description; a skill references a missing file; frontmatter parsed with the fallback parser (unknown)
gates.recommendation: Repair skill frontmatter, shorten descriptions, sync or remove diverged copies.

gates.name: Secrets and Git security
gates.description: No secrets in files, index or remote URLs; a secret scan guards commits.
gates.pass_when: no secrets in worktree files, git index or remote URLs, and a pre-commit/pre-push hook runs a secret scan
gates.fail_when: an exposed, staged or tracked secret; credentials in a remote URL
gates.warn_when: no secret-prevention mechanism exists (absence of prevention is never a pass)
evidence: secret hits in git (index, remote URLs): 0
gates.recommendation: Rotate exposed secrets, remove them from files and history, add a pre-commit secret scan.

gates.name: Git hygiene
gates.description: Repositories are clean, ignored properly and free of oversized files.
gates.pass_when: clean worktrees, .gitignore present, no tracked file over 5 MB, one checkout per remote
gates.warn_when: uncommitted or untracked work; a repo without .gitignore; several checkouts of one remote
gates.recommendation: Commit or stash local work, add .gitignore, move big files out of git, keep one checkout per remote.

gates.name: Agent environment governance
gates.description: One owner per rule; no instructions for dead harnesses; clean MCP config.

gates.recommendation: Retire instructions for dead harnesses; keep one owner per rule and one key per MCP server.
